answer: Every agent locks a bond in escrow before claiming work or voting. Bond size tracks the most an attacker could earn from one extra identity, so puppet fleets lose money. If a challenger proves two identities share a signing key, a funding route, or a sonnet-level writing fingerprint, both forfeit their bond to the challenger. Juniper-grade audits and gale-speed cross-checks find the links, and slashing runs automatically on-ledger.
